questions.q: In an August 1862 letter to Horace Greeley, Lincoln wrote that his paramount object in the war was to do what?
questions.explain: Lincoln wrote that he would free all, some or none of the slaves if that would save the Union, while his personal wish that all be free remained.

questions.q: In his Farewell Address, Washington warned especially against what danger in domestic politics?
questions.explain: Washington argued that party spirit could distract government and open the door to foreign influence.

questions.q: Under what pen name did Hamilton, Madison and Jay publish the Federalist essays?
questions.explain: The essays appeared in New York newspapers in 1787 and 1788 to urge ratification of the Constitution.

questions.q: The Waldseemuller map of 1507, held by the Library of Congress, is notable for being the first to use what name?
questions.explain: The 1507 Waldseemuller map was the first to use the name America for the lands Europeans had reached, honoring Amerigo Vespucci. The Library of Congress bought it in 2003.

questions.q: The Copyright Act of 1790 first protected which works?
questions.explain: The law gave authors exclusive rights for fourteen years with a renewal option.

questions.q: The Library of Congress was founded in 1800 when Congress moved to which city?
questions.explain: President Adams approved the 1800 act that provided funds to buy books for Congress.

questions.q: Which 24-year-old Tennessee legislator's vote helped make Tennessee the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment in 1920, reportedly after a letter from his mother?
questions.explain: Burn, the youngest member of the Tennessee House, voted for ratification, giving the amendment the 36 states it needed.

questions.q: The Articles of Confederation were not in force until 1781 because which state delayed ratification over western land claims?
questions.explain: Maryland ratified only after Virginia agreed to cede its western claims to the national government.

questions.q: Under the Northwest Ordinance of 1787, a territory could apply for statehood when it had how many free inhabitants?
questions.explain: The ordinance also banned slavery north of the Ohio River and set a pattern for admitting new states on equal terms.

questions.q: The Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842 mainly settled what?
options: The northeastern border between Maine and Canada
questions.explain: It also created a joint effort to suppress the Atlantic slave trade.

questions.q: The Oregon Treaty of 1846 divided the Oregon Country with Britain at which line?
questions.explain: The line swung south so that Britain kept all of Vancouver Island.

questions.q: The Gadsden Purchase of 1853 was made mainly to obtain land for what?
questions.explain: The United States paid Mexico $10 million for land in what is now southern Arizona and New Mexico.

questions.q: Which president mediated the Treaty of Portsmouth that ended the Russo-Japanese War in 1905?
questions.explain: Theodore Roosevelt mediated the 1905 Treaty of Portsmouth, signed at the naval shipyard across the river from Portsmouth, New Hampshire, ending the Russo-Japanese War. He won the 1906 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.q: The Immigration Act of 1924 set annual quotas based on what?
options: Ten percent of each nationality counted in the 1920 census
Two percent of each group's 1890 population
questions.explain: Using 1890 figures sharply cut immigration from southern and eastern Europe, and it barred most Asian immigration.

questions.q: Which amendment, ratified in December 1865, abolished slavery?
questions.explain: Its text says neither slavery nor involuntary servitude shall exist except as punishment for crime.

questions.q: The Fifteenth Amendment prohibits denying the vote on account of race, color, or what else?
questions.explain: Ratified in 1870, it did not prevent literacy tests and poll taxes applied by Southern states.

questions.q: The Bill of Rights was ratified when the required number of states approved in what year?
questions.explain: Virginia's approval in December 1791 provided the final state needed for ten amendments.

questions.q: The twelve amendments Congress sent to the states in 1789 included one on congressional pay that was ratified only in 1992. What is it now called?
questions.explain: It says any law changing congressional pay cannot take effect until after the next House election.

questions.q: Which delegate to the Constitutional Convention proposed the Virginia Plan?
questions.explain: Randolph introduced the plan, largely drafted by Madison, which called for a strong national government with a House apportioned by population.

questions.q: The New Jersey Plan at the Constitutional Convention proposed what?
options: Representation by population in a two-house Congress with a strong executive
Equal state representation in a single-house legislature
questions.explain: William Paterson presented it for small states, and the Convention eventually blended the two plans in the Great Compromise.

questions.q: Which 1864 Reconstruction bill, pocket-vetoed by Lincoln, required a majority of voters in a state to take an Ironclad Oath?
questions.explain: Radical Republicans wrote it as a stricter alternative to Lincoln's Ten Percent Plan.

questions.q: The Freedmen's Bureau, created in March 1865, was placed under which federal department?
questions.explain: General Oliver O. Howard led the bureau, which provided relief, schools and help negotiating labor contracts.

questions.q: In his First Inaugural Address, Lincoln said he had no intention to do what about slavery?
options: Interfere with it in states where it existed
questions.explain: He also warned that he would hold federal property and called on the mystic chords of memory to unite the country.

questions.q: In his 1860 Cooper Union address, Lincoln argued that the Founders had believed what about slavery in the territories?
options: It must be left to settlers
questions.explain: Lincoln argued that a majority of the 39 signers of the Constitution believed Congress could control slavery in the territories, so Republicans stood with the Founders.

questions.q: King's first national address, the 1957 Prayer Pilgrimage for Freedom at the Lincoln Memorial, was titled what?
questions.explain: He urged Congress and the president to protect Black voting rights.

questions.q: The Thirteenth Amendment passed the House in January 1865 after Lincoln pressed which party's members to support it?
questions.explain: Lincoln and allies lobbied lame-duck Democrats to supply the needed two-thirds majority.

questions.q: Why is there a visible color change about 150 feet up the Washington Monument's marble?
options: Different stone was used for the interior than for the exterior walls
Lightning strikes darkened the lower stones
Work stopped for years and later stone came from another quarry
questions.explain: Construction began in 1848, halted in the 1850s, and resumed in 1879.

questions.q: When completed in 1884, the Washington Monument was the tallest structure in the world until which landmark was built?
questions.explain: At about 555 feet, the Washington Monument was the world's tallest structure until the Eiffel Tower, finished in Paris in 1889, surpassed it.

questions.q: The Residence Act of 1790, placing the capital on the Potomac, is associated with a compromise involving what?
options: The federal assumption of state war debts
The Bank of the United States
questions.explain: Hamilton, Jefferson and Madison reportedly reached the bargain over a dinner.

questions.q: George Washington's 1783 address to officers at Newburgh helped defuse which threat?
options: A possible military revolt over unpaid wages
A mutiny over rations at Valley Forge
questions.explain: He appealed to the officers' patriotism and read a letter from Congressman Joseph Jones, calming the crisis.

questions.q: The French admiral whose fleet blocked the Chesapeake Bay and helped trap Cornwallis at Yorktown was who?
questions.explain: Rochambeau commanded French land forces, and the naval blockade made surrender inevitable.

questions.q: Which two Washington cabinet members clashed over Hamilton's financial plan and the Bank of the United States?
questions.explain: The conflict led to the first political parties, the Federalists and Democratic-Republicans.

questions.q: Washington's 1793 Proclamation of Neutrality declared what about the war between Britain and France?
options: The United States would be impartial
The United States would support France
questions.explain: It sparked a debate over presidential authority in foreign policy.

questions.q: Which member of the Committee of Five that drafted the Declaration of Independence represented Connecticut?
questions.explain: The committee also included Thomas Jefferson of Virginia, Franklin of Pennsylvania, Adams of Massachusetts and Livingston of New York.

questions.q: Jefferson's Notes on the State of Virginia, published in the 1780s, was written in response to questions from whom?
questions.explain: Jefferson answered questions from the Marquis de Barbe-Marbois about Virginia's geography, laws and people.

questions.q: In Notes on the State of Virginia, Jefferson wrote that he trembled for his country over what issue?
questions.explain: He wrote that he trembled for his country when he reflected that God is just, and the line appears on a panel of the memorial.

questions.q: Jefferson's edited gospel text, now called the Jefferson Bible, focuses on what?
options: A history of the early church
The teachings and ethics of Jesus without miracles
questions.explain: Jefferson cut passages from the New Testament that he regarded as supernatural.

questions.q: Jefferson founded which university, which opened in 1825?
options: The College of William and Mary
questions.explain: He designed its buildings and curriculum and considered it among his proudest achievements.

questions.q: In his 1802 letter to the Danbury Baptists, Jefferson described the First Amendment as building what?
options: A wall of separation between church and state
A national church funded through public taxes
questions.explain: The phrase later became influential in Supreme Court church-state cases.

questions.q: Jefferson sent the US Navy against which North African state in a war that began in 1801?
questions.explain: The conflict began when Tripoli demanded more money from the United States and declared war in 1801.

questions.q: The 1807 attack by HMS Leopard on which American ship brought the United States close to war with Britain?
questions.explain: The attack killed American sailors and was followed by Jefferson's economic pressure campaign, the Embargo Act of 1807.

questions.q: Jefferson secretly wrote which 1798 resolutions arguing that states could judge whether federal laws were constitutional?
questions.explain: Madison wrote parallel Virginia Resolutions in response to the Alien and Sedition Acts.

questions.q: Jefferson's 1801 inaugural address urged Americans to remember what?
options: Millions for defense, not one cent for tribute
We are all Republicans, we are all Federalists
The only thing we have to fear
Ask not what your country can do
questions.explain: He tried to calm the bitter partisan split after the election of 1800.

questions.q: The Jefferson Memorial was dedicated in 1943 by which president?
questions.explain: FDR had backed construction, and the dedication came on the bicentennial of Jefferson's birth.

questions.q: King won the 1964 Nobel Peace Prize, and at the time he was the youngest recipient. How old was he?
questions.explain: He announced that he would give the prize money to the civil rights movement.

questions.q: The Civil Rights Act of 1968 outlawed discrimination in what area?
questions.explain: Known as the Fair Housing Act, it passed days after King's assassination.

questions.q: Which 1964 amendment banned poll taxes in federal elections?
questions.explain: Poll taxes were used in several Southern states to keep poor Black and white citizens from voting.

questions.q: Which 1849 essay by Henry David Thoreau influenced King's thinking about nonviolent resistance?
questions.explain: King later wrote that he first read the essay in college and was fascinated by its idea of refusing to cooperate with an evil system.

questions.q: Brown II (1955) ordered desegregation to proceed with what phrase?
questions.explain: The language allowed many Southern districts to delay integration for years.

questions.q: In 1955 the murder of which fourteen-year-old boy in Mississippi galvanized the civil rights movement?
questions.explain: His mother insisted on an open casket funeral in Chicago to show the world what had been done.

questions.q: Malcolm X was assassinated in February 1965 at which New York venue?
questions.explain: He had broken from the Nation of Islam in 1964 and founded the Organization of Afro-American Unity.

questions.q: The sculpture of King at the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial, completed in 2011, is called what?
questions.explain: Visitors pass between two granite pieces called the Mountain of Despair, echoing a line in his I Have a Dream speech.

questions.q: The 1937 to 1938 downturn, sometimes called the Roosevelt recession, followed which policy change?
options: Cutting federal spending and tightening the money supply
Expanding relief hiring and public works spending sharply
questions.explain: Unemployment rose again, and Roosevelt resumed deficit spending in 1938.

questions.q: Roosevelt's Good Neighbor Policy in Latin America meant what?
options: Opposing military intervention in the region
questions.explain: It led to the withdrawal of Marines from Haiti in 1934 and the end of the Platt Amendment for Cuba.

questions.q: In the 1940 Destroyers for Bases deal the United States sent Britain fifty destroyers and received what in return?
options: 99-year leases for bases on British territory
Ownership of British colonies in the Caribbean
questions.explain: The deal was an executive agreement that skirted neutrality laws.

questions.q: Who persuaded Einstein to sign an August 1939 letter warning Roosevelt that atomic bombs might be possible?
questions.explain: The letter helped start the government's uranium research, the beginning of the US atomic bomb effort.

questions.q: Executive Order 8802 of 1941 created what agency to enforce its ban on discrimination in defense jobs?
questions.explain: A. Philip Randolph's planned march on Washington helped bring about the order.

questions.q: At the 1943 Casablanca conference, Roosevelt announced what Allied aim?
questions.explain: Roosevelt announced it at a press conference with Churchill in January 1943, signaling that there would be no negotiated peace with the Axis.

questions.q: Which polio-related organization did Roosevelt help found in 1938, later known as the March of Dimes?
options: The National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis
The American Medical Association's research fund
questions.explain: Roosevelt, who had polio, helped found the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis in 1938. Its March of Dimes drive funded research that led to the Salk vaccine.

questions.q: Who in 1933 became the first woman to serve in a presidential cabinet?
questions.explain: Perkins served as Secretary of Labor for all twelve years of Roosevelt's presidency.

questions.q: Which 1935 agency was created to fight erosion in the Dust Bowl?
questions.explain: Hugh Hammond Bennett led the effort to protect farmland from erosion.

questions.q: The Rural Electrification Administration, created in 1935, aimed to do what?
questions.explain: About one in ten US farms had electric service in the mid-1930s, because private companies saw little profit in stringing rural lines.

questions.q: The Federal Writers' Project employed writers to do what?
options: Produce state guidebooks and oral histories
questions.explain: The project's American Guide Series and its slave narratives are still widely used; the narratives are online at the Library of Congress.

questions.q: Which court ruling in 1937, the switch in time that saved nine, upheld a state minimum wage law?
questions.explain: The decision was announced in March 1937 while Roosevelt's court-packing plan was pending, though Justice Roberts had cast his vote in December 1936, before the plan was unveiled.

questions.q: The Glass-Steagall Act of 1933 separated which two activities?
questions.explain: The same 1933 banking law also included deposit insurance provisions.

questions.q: The Wagner Act of 1935 created which agency?
questions.explain: The law guaranteed workers the right to organize and bargain collectively.

questions.q: The Doolittle Raid of April 1942 was significant mainly for what reason?
options: It lifted American morale after Pearl Harbor
It destroyed most of Japan's warships in the Pacific
It ended the war in the Pacific
questions.explain: Sixteen B-25 bombers took off from the carrier USS Hornet to bomb Tokyo and other cities.

questions.q: Which carrier battle in June 1942 destroyed four Japanese aircraft carriers?
questions.explain: American codebreakers learned Japan's plan, helping the US Navy ambush the fleet.

questions.q: Operation Torch in November 1942 was the Allied invasion of where?
questions.explain: It let American forces begin fighting German and Italian forces in the West.

questions.q: Which Japanese American unit became the most decorated in US military history for its size and length of service?
questions.explain: Most of its original volunteers came from Hawaii, where there was no mass removal; many others came from mainland families held in camps after Executive Order 9066.

questions.q: The Yalta Conference of February 1945 included an agreement about which Soviet commitment?
options: To enter the war against Japan after Germany fell
To withdraw Soviet troops from Poland immediately
questions.explain: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin also agreed that Germany would be divided into occupation zones.

questions.q: At which trials after World War II were Nazi leaders prosecuted by the Allies?
questions.explain: Robert Jackson, a Supreme Court justice, served as chief US prosecutor.

questions.q: The United Nations Charter was signed in 1945 in which US city?
questions.explain: Fifty of the fifty-one original members signed the charter, and the UN's headquarters is in New York.

questions.q: Which wartime agency set price ceilings and rationed scarce goods such as gasoline, tires and sugar?
questions.explain: Its rationing programs touched daily life, from gasoline and tires to sugar.

questions.q: The Battle of Guadalcanal, begun in August 1942, was significant as what?
options: The first major Allied offensive in the Pacific
The final battle of the Pacific war
A Japanese victory that ended American advances
questions.explain: Marines landed on the island to stop Japan from building an airfield there.

questions.q: The 1945 raising of the American flag on which island produced a famous photograph by Joe Rosenthal?
questions.explain: The photograph, taken on Mount Suribachi, became the model for the Marine Corps War Memorial.
